canonicalIngredients.name: cooked long grain white rice, day-old
bacon / ham / char siu pork
observations: 300 g char siu pork, or bacon (s0)

causalSequence: cook rice ahead; chill overnight so grains dry and separate
stage all ingredients in bowls; mix sauce before heat goes on
heat wok until smoking; crisp bacon (or warm ham / char siu), remove
scramble eggs in the wok, or later in a well in the rice; set aside
stir-fry onion, carrot, garlic, ginger 1-3 min until fragrant
add prawns; fry ~1 min until just pink (pre-cooked prawns only need warming)
add cold rice; toss on high heat 2-3 min, breaking clumps
add peas; fold egg and bacon back through
add soy, sesame oil, oyster sauce; toss 1-2 min until rice starts to catch
finish with spring onion; serve immediately
techniqueFacts: all four sources use cold day-old rice — fresh rice steams and clumps
three sources cook egg separately (or in a well) then fold back so curds stay distinct
smoking-hot wok with everything prepped first is the fry-not-steam lever (two sources state it explicitly)
pork element varies: char siu (s0, notes bacon or 175 g Chinese sausage swap), bacon (s1), deli ham (s2), leg ham (s3)
raw prawns get ~1 min to pink (s0); pre-cooked prawns are only warmed through (s3)
soy sauce is the one universal seasoning; sesame oil appears in three sources; one source adds oyster/hoisin/butter (s1), one builds a jug sauce with fish sauce, shaoxing and stock (s0)
one source rinses rice until water runs clear before cooking to cut starch (s3); s0 echoes washing to avoid clumping
